name: VitaSeq
description: VitaSeq is developing a blood-based diagnostic test that uses a patented microRNA signature to detect Alzheimer's-associated cognitive decline years before symptom onset. The test produces a cognition score reflecting brain health, targeting the early Alzheimer's detection market where current gold-standard diagnostics (CSF and PET) are invasive, costly, and used too late.
team: Pitch presented by Florian Erber to Ananda Impact Ventures; founding team details not specified in the deck, though the underlying microRNA signature science was published in EMBO Molecular Medicine (Islam et al. 2021).

name: Cardiovolt.ai
description: Cardiovolt.ai provides Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) that uses AI to detect hidden heart disease in standard ECGs, identifying 14 cardiac and 3 non-cardiac conditions before symptoms appear. The company sells B2B to healthcare providers and pharma/life sciences companies, targeting the 1B+ ECGs performed globally each year to enable proactive cardiac care and enrich clinical trials.
team: The pitch deck does not provide specific details on the founding team or their backgrounds.

name: HotHouse Therapeutics
description: HotHouseTx is a spin-out from the John Innes Centre's Osbourn Lab that combines AI-driven drug design (BotanAI) with a plant-based bioproduction platform (BotanBio) to design, make, and test complex natural product-like compounds on drug-discovery timelines. Its initial focus is on next-generation vaccine adjuvants, with a broader vision of sustainable, plant-made therapeutics.
team: Led by CEO Dr David Sheppard (ex-EntactBio founder, 26 years in biotech) and CSO Professor Anne Osbourn OBE FRS (world leader in plant metabolic engineering), with Dr Phil Spence heading informatics and Ivan Griffin (ex-BenevolentAI) as CBO/Co-Founder. Advised by Adrian Hill of the Jenner Institute.

name: Sapio Health
description: Sapio Health is building Horizon-1, a continuous physics engine for human health that fuses multi-modal clinical and wearable data to model disease trajectories over time. It serves both clinicians (via detection, coding, and messaging interfaces sold to providers) and patients (via a freemium app), targeting the chronic disease and primary care market in the UK and US.
team: The pitch deck does not provide explicit details about the founding team or their backgrounds.

name: VUS Genetics
description: VUS Genetics is building a proprietary functional genomics and data intelligence platform that links drug target discovery, patient stratification, and clinical outcomes to improve oncology drug development success rates. Its first product, ATMpredict, identifies ATM-mutant cancer patients who could benefit from ATR inhibitor therapies, enabling label expansion for biotech and pharma partners.
team: The team is supported by 4 international clinical research collaborators and has signed an exclusive license on a novel gene editing approach, with 9 MSAs signed with biotech and pharma partners indicating commercial traction. Specific founder backgrounds are not detailed in the deck.

name: Collo
description: Collo provides liquid process intelligence for Food & Beverage manufacturing, using a novel radio frequency-based inline liquid analyzer combined with AI/ML algorithms and a SaaS platform. The technology identifies and automates optimal operating conditions, reducing product loss, water usage, and quality-related costs in liquid processing.
team: The team is not described in the provided pitch deck excerpt.

name: Unnamed Prostate MRI Startup
description: The company is developing an autonomous, low-field MRI device focused on early detection of prostate cancer, designed to be deployed in freestanding imaging centers under a per-scan commercial model. It targets the existing ~$400M US reimbursed prostate MRI pathway, with plans to expand into broader screening as guidelines evolve.
team: The founding team is not described in the provided pitch deck text, so relevant backgrounds cannot be summarized.

name: Health Concierge
description: Health Concierge offers an AI-powered hospital discharge platform that automates patient transition tasks—like finding specialists, verifying availability, and generating paperwork—to reduce discharge delays. Targeting US hospitals facing a $100B care transition inefficiency problem, the platform embeds into existing clinical workflows to free beds, cut costs, and improve patient outcomes.
team: The team is supported by a roster of advisors including Cynthia Henderson PhD, Erin Donnelly, Gary Paquin, Justin Force, Nigel Daniels, Duane Cooney, Trista Taylor, Denis Victor, and Khalid Turk, and has assembled a nationwide consulting team of 6 industry experts covering most of the US.

name: POSTMAN (by the team behind POSTMAN-1)
description: The company builds foundation models that generate missing patient biological data from existing measurements, predicting one modality (e.g., spatial proteomics markers like CD20, PD-L1, LAG3) from another (e.g., H&E slides). Their first model, POSTMAN-1, is a 1B-parameter in silico spatial proteomics model aimed at the pharma R&D and multimodal patient data market, competing in a space led by players like Tempus.
team: Founded by CEO Yue Dai, formerly core technical staff on the $400M Pathos–AstraZeneca deal and IEEE-published, and CTO Oded Falik, who built Enable Medicine's spatial biology platform scaled to 12B+ single-cell annotations. Both have deep technical backgrounds in AI and multimodal biological data.

name: Vitroscope
description: Vitroscope builds a patented perfusion-based phenotyping platform that keeps human organoids, tissues, and cell models viable and physiologically relevant in the lab for longer than existing methods. It targets the pharma drug R&D market, replacing inaccurate well plates and animal models with humanized in vitro systems for screening, discovery, and optimization.
team: Founded by three PhDs covering complementary domains: CEO Carlo Kriesi (biomedical engineering, ETH Zurich/CERN), CTO Heikki Sjöman (IoT/mechatronics, Aalto/Stanford), and CBDO Sandra Jernström (tissue/oncology postdoc, ex-CSO of Okomera). Backed by advisors from Emerald Cloud Labs, Charles River Laboratories, KPMG, and the University of Oxford.
